scope.summary: Implement jiggle-bone secondary-motion chain generation per Section 13.18 (BK-18.4, TAI-BK-069), closing GREQ-023: secondary-motion bone chains for breasts, glutes, belly, cock, and balls generated MECHANICALLY from region masks + channel state (volume/firmness), with per-chain parameters (stiffness, damping, gravity response, limits); generated chains are ordinary skeleton-def bones (exportable) and the bake target for 13.20 soft-tissue keyframe baking.
acceptance_criteria: generate_jiggle_chains(region_masks, channel_state) emits bone chains for breast_l/r, glute_l/r, belly, penis, and scrotum regions with chain length/placement derived from region extent (bigger volume -> longer/deeper chain placement) — derivation is mechanical, no hand-authored per-body chains.

Per-chain JiggleParams {stiffness, damping, gravity_response, limits} derive from the physics-coupled channels: breast_firmness at 1.0 (implant) yields measurably stiffer/more-damped params than 0.0 (natural soft) at equal volume (TAI-BK-040 mechanical link test).
Generated chains splice into the skeleton def as ordinary exportable bones under a minor version bump (TAI-BK-058); they respect canonical naming (breast_jiggle_01_l style snake_case).

Regeneration on channel change is deterministic and idempotent: same channel state regenerates identical chains; changed volume updates placement without orphaning previously generated bones (replace semantics).
Generated params serialize into the structure the MT-526 physics sidecar consumes (typed handshake between the two MTs).
scope.risk_if_missed: Daz has NO native soft-body and its jiggle aftermarket exists because bones must be hand-added per figure; if chains are hand-authored instead of channel-derived, every archetype needs custom rig work and the firmness channel's natural-vs-implant motion contract (OBR-001) silently breaks.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
